clauses: Draw/move order; fighters and allowance; passage/blocking/occupied space; no interleaving.
answers.answer: Draw first; finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

evidence.text: 1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

clauses: BOOST payment/value; discarded effect; each fighter; defeated fighter card eligibility.
answers.answer: Each of your fighters gets the allowance; a defeated fighter’s card can still pay BOOST.

evidence.text: **BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Empty deck mandatory draw two; no reshuffle/decline; damage per survivor.

clauses: Melee/ranged legal target cases across/shared/disconnected zones.
answers.answer: Both may attack an adjacent opponent across zones; only ranged can attack nonadjacent opponents in a shared zone, even disconnected parts.

evidence.text: One fighter per circular space. Spaces connected by a line are **adjacent**. A **zone** consists of all spaces with the same colored pattern, even if separated on the board. A space showing several patterns belongs to all those zones. Adjacency and shared zones are different tests.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.
2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.
3. **Resolve combat** in the order below, then discard played cards to their owners’ **face-up discard piles**.

clauses: Combat order; defender first at same timing; mandatory effects unless optional; other effects and discard piles.
answers.answer: Resolve same-timing effects defender first; effects are mandatory unless stated otherwise.

evidence.text: ### Combat timing, damage and winning combat

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

clauses: Attack 4 vs defense 4 then effect damage: winner/reason; no defense damage.
answers.answer: Defender wins since attack damage is zero; effect damage does not change winner. No defense means 4 attack damage.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

answers.answer: Remove sidekick token; its card effect resolves if duel continues. Hero reaching zero ends duel immediately; healing cannot undo it.

evidence.text: There is no points score. Any fighter reduced to **zero health for any reason is defeated**. Immediately remove a defeated sidekick token. A Harpy is defeated by any damage because it has 1 health.

clauses: Scheme action/resolution; defeated restriction; discard inspection.
answers.answer: Play face up, declare an allowed active fighter, resolve, then discard. Both players may inspect either face-up discard pile any time.

evidence.text: Play a scheme (yellow lightning icon) from hand **face up**, declaring a fighter allowed by its fighter label as the **active fighter**. You cannot play a scheme if its listed fighters are defeated. Resolve its effect, then put it in your discard pile.
- Played and resolved cards and discarded cards go into your own **face-up discard pile**, distinct from the face-down deck. Both players may inspect either discard pile **at any time**.

clauses: Alice health, attack, move; Jabberwock stats; size selection and bonuses; bonus applicability.
answers.answer: Alice’s controller chooses BIG or SMALL at setup; the size bonuses apply to Alice, not Jabberwock.

evidence.text: | Hero | Starting health | Attack | Move | Sidekick(s): starting health, attack |
| Alice | 13 | Melee | 2 | Jabberwock: 8, melee |

**Alice:** choose BIG or SMALL when placing her at setup. When **BIG**, add **2 to Alice’s attack-card values**. When **SMALL**, add **1 to Alice’s defense-card values**. This includes versatile cards used in that role. These bonuses belong to **Alice, not Jabberwock**. “Change size” switches BIG ↔ SMALL and updates the token; it is mandatory when the effect says so. After-combat size changes occur after the current combat result and do not retroactively change its damage.

clauses: Arthur/Merlin health, attack types, move; Arthur BOOST timing/method/cancel consequence.
answers.answer: Arthur may BOOST when attacking by playing a hand card face down alongside his attack; canceled effects discard the BOOST without effect.

evidence.text: | Hero | Starting health | Attack | Move | Sidekick(s): starting health, attack |
| King Arthur | 18 | Melee | 2 | Merlin: 7, ranged |

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.

clauses: Sinbad/Porter stats and move; 3 Voyage maneuver bonus; Voyage value and self-count.
answers.answer: Each moves 2 + 3 = 5. Voyage value is 2 + 3 already discarded = 5; the played Voyage is not yet in discard.

evidence.text: | Hero | Starting health | Attack | Move | Sidekick(s): starting health, attack |
| Sinbad | 15 | Melee | 2 | Porter: 6, melee |

**Sinbad:** when you maneuver, each of your fighters may move **+1 space for each VOYAGE card in your discard pile**, added to the normal move value 2 and any maneuver BOOST. The bonus also applies to Porter. The maneuver allowance is **2 + Voyages currently in discard + the chosen maneuver BOOST value**. Count the Voyages actually in the discard pile when moving: if Voyage Home is discarded to BOOST this maneuver, it counts in **both applicable terms**: +1 for being a Voyage in discard and +1 from its printed BOOST value.

All **7 Voyage** cards are **Sinbad-only attack cards, printed combat value 2, one copy each**. **Voyage Home has BOOST 1; the other six have no printed BOOST value.** Each has: **during combat, add 1 value for every Voyage card already in your discard pile**. Thus the normal value is **2 + that existing pile count**; exclude only the card currently being played because it is not in discard yet. **Three already-discarded Voyages give value 5.** Their separate after-combat effects are below; they **do not require winning** unless an effect explicitly says so.

clauses: Voyage Home value; other Voyage cards retrieval and destination; Home destination; next maneuver.
answers.answer: Value 2 + 4 = 6. Retrieve other Voyages to hand; Home remains in discard. Next allowance is 2 + 1 = 3.

evidence.text: All **7 Voyage** cards are **Sinbad-only attack cards, printed combat value 2, one copy each**. **Voyage Home has BOOST 1; the other six have no printed BOOST value.** Each has: **during combat, add 1 value for every Voyage card already in your discard pile**. Thus the normal value is **2 + that existing pile count**; exclude only the card currently being played because it is not in discard yet. **Three already-discarded Voyages give value 5.** Their separate after-combat effects are below; they **do not require winning** unless an effect explicitly says so.
| Voyage | After combat (only while the duel continues) |

| Voyage Home | Take all **other Voyage cards from your discard pile into hand**. Then Home itself goes to discard at the normal end of combat. The retrieved cards leave the pile, but **Home remains there**: with Home alone in discard, each fighter’s next unboosted maneuver allowance is **2 + 1 = 3**, not 2. |

**Sinbad:** when you maneuver, each of your fighters may move **+1 space for each VOYAGE card in your discard pile**, added to the normal move value 2 and any maneuver BOOST. The bonus also applies to Porter. The maneuver allowance is **2 + Voyages currently in discard + the chosen maneuver BOOST value**. Count the Voyages actually in the discard pile when moving: if Voyage Home is discarded to BOOST this maneuver, it counts in **both applicable terms**: +1 for being a Voyage in discard and +1 from its printed BOOST value.

**Voyage combat values:** during combat, a Voyage’s printed effect adds **1 for every Voyage card already in your discard pile** to its printed value 2. In formula form, **combat value = 2 + the number of Voyages already in discard**, before other modifiers. Count **every Voyage already there**; the card being played is not yet in that pile and therefore does not count itself. Its absence does not remove any of the cards already discarded. For example, with **3 Voyages already in discard**, the new Voyage has value **2 + 3 = 5**, not 2. Resolve this bonus during combat before calculating damage. Played cards enter discard only at the end of combat. Voyage Home’s later after-combat retrieval can reduce the count for later combats or maneuvers.
